precepts.text: Some people's iniquity will not be purged until they die; do not be the example God has to make.
precepts.point: The only way the wickedness of the wicked comes to an end is that they die. The wicked is the so-called white man according to the bible, and his end is inevitable. This is God's word, not man's; do not try to get God's enemy out of the way.

note.label: Psalm 7: David's Prayer for Deliverance in the Last Days

precepts.why:
David asks, “Oh let the wickedness of the wicked come to an end”. The only way the wickedness of the wicked comes to an end is that they die. Isaiah heard it from the Lord: “And it was revealed in mine ears by the Lord of hosts, Surely this iniquity shall not be purged from you till ye die, saith the Lord God of hosts.”

Some people's iniquity will not be purged until they die. That is why the wicked must come to an end for the wickedness to end. Do not be the example God has to make.

David says “the righteous God trieth the hearts and reins.” God judges the thoughts, so we must change our mindset and move forward in righteousness, so that our iniquity is purged by repentance and not by death.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 3 A Message to The 7 Churches

precepts.why:
Here is the prophecy on the key of David. Christ is the one that is holy and true; he is the one that has the key of David. “And the key of the house of David will I lay upon his shoulder; so he shall open, and none shall shut; and he shall shut, and none shall open.” You know what that is going into? Salvation. If the Lord is opening up this word to you, no man can close it. If God is opening up your spirit to what this Bible is saying, he is bringing you into this truth, he has called you, and nobody can do anything about that. But if he shuts you out because of your wicked self, there is nothing we can do to help you. There is another scripture where Paul said it is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the Most High. There is nothing we can do to help you. So all you turncoats, all you traitors out there, remember this word.

Read from verse 20 so nobody reads above it and says, what's this? “And it shall come to pass in that day, that I will call my servant Eliakim the son of Hilkiah:” Eliakim, the son of Hilkiah, lived during this time; he was a disciple of Isaiah, and Eliakim means resurrection of God. So this is really a metaphor about Christ. “And I will clothe him with thy robe, and strengthen him with thy girdle, and I will commit thy government into his hand: and he shall be a father to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and to the house of Judah. And the key of the house of David will I lay upon his shoulder; so he shall open, and none shall shut; and he shall shut, and none shall open.”

“And I will fasten him as a nail in a sure place;” Christ is fastened as a nail in a sure place, meaning you can't budge him, you can't move him. “and he shall be for a glorious throne to his father’s house.”

note.label: In a Game of Fools Without The Rules

points: The Lord will carry thee away with a mighty captivity, and will surely violently turn and toss thee like a ball into a large country. Like lottery balls in the jar: that was us on the slave ship for months, rocking on planks, sick and soiled on one another, from the west coast of Africa into North America, the last slave trade.
There shalt thou die, in a land you do not know, as a slave and a subject.

note.label: There Is No Hate Like Christian Love

points: The burden of the valley of vision falls on a city gone up to the housetops, a tumultuous and once joyous city whose slain men are not slain with the sword nor dead in battle. Its rulers are fled together and bound, and the prophet turns away to weep bitterly and will not be comforted.

note.label: Isaiah 22: The Burden of the Valley of Vision

points: It is a day of trouble, of treading down, and of perplexity by the Most High of hosts in the valley of vision, with the walls broken down and a crying to the mountains. Elam bears the quiver with chariots of men and horsemen, and Kir uncovers the shield, so the choicest valleys are full of chariots set in array at the gate.

note.label: Isaiah 22: The Burden of the Valley of Vision

points: The people look to their defenses in that day: the breaches of the city of David, the gathering of the waters of the lower pool, the numbering and breaking down of houses to fortify the wall, and a ditch made between the two walls for the water of the old pool. Yet they have not looked unto the Maker thereof nor had respect unto Him that fashioned it long ago.

note.label: Isaiah 22: The Burden of the Valley of Vision

points: In that day the Most High of hosts calls to weeping, mourning, baldness, and girding with sackcloth, but instead there is joy and gladness, slaying oxen and eating flesh, saying "let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we shall die." The Most High reveals that this iniquity shall not be purged from them till they die.

note.label: Isaiah 22: The Burden of the Valley of Vision

points: The word comes against Shebna, the treasurer over the house, who has hewn himself out a sepulchre on high and graved a habitation for himself in a rock. The Most High will carry him away with a mighty captivity, toss him like a ball into a large country where he shall die, and drive him from his station and pull him down from his state.

note.label: Isaiah 22: The Burden of the Valley of Vision

points: In Shebna's place the Most High calls His servant Eliakim the son of Hilkiah, clothing him with the robe and girdle and committing the government into his hand, so he is a father to Jerusalem and to Judah with the key of the house of David laid upon his shoulder to open and shut. He is fastened as a nail in a sure place for a glorious throne, yet in that day the nail shall be removed, cut down, and fall, and the burden upon it cut off.
